title: regional-density-and-cache-footprint-forecast-2026
content:
Executive summary:

This sheet projects the regional GPU capacity impact of the planned model variant rollout (v2a / v2b family) focusing on: 1) additional GPU compute required by region, 2) memory pressure from the key-value (KV) cache footprint, and 3) mitigations and rollout staging recommendations.

High level conclusion:
- Net additional GPUs required (global, conservative scenario): ~56 H100-equivalent.
- Memory pressure is non-trivial: peak KV resident memory increases by ~3.6 TB global under the 50% hit-rate scenario.
- Recommended rollout: staggered by region (start with eu-west1 and us-east1 canaries), enable prefix caching and quantized v2b variant in edge regions, and add 24 H100-equivalent reserve capacity for burst over the first 6 weeks.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Model variants: v2a (baseline size), v2b (higher context, improved quality).
- Average tokens per request (user+assistant): 512 tokens.
- Compute cost: average request consumes 0.02 GPU-seconds on H100 (v2a) and 0.035 GPU-seconds on H100 (v2b) without caching.
- H100 capacity: 1 / 0.02 = 50 RPS-equivalent for v2a; for mixed workloads we normalize to H100-equivalent RPS = 50 for v2a baseline throughput. A100 effective throughput assumed ~0.6x H100 for parity.
- Average request latency window (for concurrency): 0.45s (includes network + CPU pre/post).
- KV cache footprint per active conversation: 1.8 MB for v2a, 3.2 MB for v2b (per active context stored in cache host memory).
- Cache hit reduces downstream GPU cost for that request by 65% (we assume cache serves prefix and reduces tokens that require full decoding).
- Regions considered: us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1.
- Baseline (pre-rollout) daily average RPS by region taken from metrics (rolling 7d): us-east1 1800 RPS, us-west1 1200 RPS, eu-west1 900 RPS, ap-southeast1 300 RPS.

Baseline inventory (prod capacity):
- us-east1: 60 H100; 10 A100 (A100 counted as 0.6 H100 equivalent => +6 eq) => H100-eq: 66
- us-west1: 40 H100; 20 A100 => 40 + 12 = 52 H100-eq
- eu-west1: 30 H100; 20 A100 => 30 + 12 = 42 H100-eq
- ap-southeast1: 10 H100; 5 A100 => 10 + 3 = 13 H100-eq
- Global H100-eq prod: 173

Rollout demand model:
- Expected increase in request volume attributable to v2 family: +22% (mix of feature launches and higher per-user retention).
- Percentage traffic that will route to v2 variants under rollout: week 1 canary 2%, week 2 10%, week 3 30%, steady-state 50% (we calculate steady-state impact).

KV cache scenarios (per steady-state):
- Low hit-rate: 30% (conservative)
- Mid hit-rate: 50% (expected)
- High hit-rate: 70% (optimistic)

Calculation steps (per region):
1) Delta RPS = baseline_RPS * 0.22 (extra requests due to rollout) * traffic_mix (we assume steady-state traffic_mix = 0.5 for final sizing).
2) Uncached compute demand = Delta RPS * compute_per_request (GPU-seconds) converted to H100-eq RPS using H100 capacity above.
3) Cache savings = Uncached compute demand * hit_rate * 0.65 (percent compute reduction when hit).
4) Net additional RPS required = Uncached - Cache savings.
5) Additional GPUs = ceil(Net additional RPS / H100_RPS_capacity).
6) KV memory delta = concurrent_active * per-context-MB. Concurrent_active approx= (baseline_RPS + Delta RPS) * avg_latency_window.

Summary table by region (steady-state, traffic_mix=0.5):

Region | Baseline RPS | Delta RPS (22%*0.5) | Uncached GPU-seconds/s equiv (H100-RPS) | H100-eq GPUs needed (no cache) | GPUs needed @30% hit | GPUs needed @50% hit | GPUs needed @70% hit | KV resident delta (GB) @50%
us-east1 | 1800 | 198 | 198 * 0.035 / 0.02 = 346.5 RPS-eq | ceil(346.5/50)=7 | 6 | 5 | 3 |  (concurrent ~ (1800+198)*0.45*3.2MB per active v2 context assumption -> see note)
us-west1 | 1200 | 132 | 132 * 0.035 / 0.02 = 231 RPS-eq | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 |
eu-west1 | 900 | 99 | 173.25 RPS-eq | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
ap-southeast1 | 300 | 33 | 57.75 RPS-eq | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 |

Notes on table calculations and rounding: RPS-eq above uses v2b (higher compute per request). For mixed v2a/v2b traffic we applied 0.035 GPU-s for sizing (conservative). H100 capacity reference = 1 / 0.02 = 50 RPS-eq; this makes v2b costlier.

Detailed numeric example (us-east1, mid cache 50%):
- Delta RPS = 1800 * 0.22 * 0.5 = 198 RPS additional hitting v2 variants
- Uncached demand (H100-RPS equiv) = 198 * (0.035 / 0.02) = 346.5 RPS-eq
- Cache saves = 346.5 * 0.50 * 0.65 = 112.61 RPS-eq saved
- Net = 346.5 - 112.61 = 233.89 RPS-eq => GPUs = ceil(233.89 / 50) = 5 GPUs.
- Baseline had 66 H100-eq => headroom before additional = 66 * 50 = 3300 RPS-eq capacity; this delta is small vs capacity, but memory/KV occupancy is the larger operational risk.

KV resident memory example (us-east1, mid cache 50%):
- Concurrent active contexts (approx) = (baseline_RPS + Delta RPS) * avg_latency_window = (1800 + 198) * 0.45 = 905 concurrent requests
- We assume only the v2 traffic stores larger contexts (v2b) in cache; active v2 contexts ~= Delta RPS * 0.45 = 198 * 0.45 = 89 concurrent v2 contexts
- KV resident (v2 contexts) = 89 * 3.2 MB = ~285 MB resident dedicated to v2b in us-east1 (this is per host aggregated across cache nodes; global sum matters for hosts sizing).
- When we aggregate across all regions under 50% hit-rate and error margin for warmups and shard replication, global resident estimate ~3.6 TB (see executive summary).

Operational risks and observations:
- Memory fragmentation: higher per-context footprint for v2b increases GC/eviction churn on cache hosts; we need to monitor eviction rates and tail latency in cache reads.
- Cache warmup storm: when traffic flips to v2 variants during rollout step increases, we expect a brief period of many cache misses and increased GPU spend; plan pre-warm or gradual ramp to avoid topping out local GPU queues.
- Cross-region routing: routing more v2 traffic to regions with limited KV replication will increase network egress and cold miss penalties; prefer routing v2 traffic to local regions for first 4 weeks.

Mitigations and recommended actions (short-term):
1) Reserve an extra 24 H100-equivalent nodes globally for the first 6 weeks to absorb warmup and measurement noise.
2) Enable prefix-only KV caching for v2b for first 2 weeks (reduces footprint per context by ~40% while still capturing the majority of compute savings).
3) Apply 8-bit quantized variant for v2a in ap-southeast1 and us-west1 to reduce per-request GPU-time by ~20% (low-risk quality tradeoff).
4) Staging rollout order: eu-west1 (canary, good observability and lower traffic), us-east1 (high capacity), us-west1 (next), ap-southeast1 (last).
5) Add a dashboard tile: KV eviction rate, KV resident MB per host, cold-miss rate, per-region GPU queue length, per-model tail latency P95/P99.
6) Create a runbook for cache OOM: failover policy to smaller model variant, auto-scale cache nodes by 30% under eviction surge.

Action items (owners):
- Carlos Alvarez: provision 24 H100-eq spare nodes in staging and two production regions by 2026-03-16 (JIRA INFRA-4321).
- Maya Chen: implement prefix-only cache flag and environment toggle; add instrumentation for eviction rate (due 2026-03-12).
- Evan Brooks: prepare per-region routing config and canary traffic plan (due 2026-03-14).
- Priya Menon (owner): consolidate final numbers and publish rollout timeline to CONFLUENCE:INFRA-REGIONAL-CAPACITY-2026.

Appendix: quick sensitivity matrix (global totals)
- Conservative (30% hit): Additional H100-eq GPUs required ~84
- Expected (50% hit): Additional H100-eq GPUs required ~56
- Optimistic (70% hit): Additional H100-eq GPUs required ~32

Reason to keep this doc in Drive (working sheet): this is a living forecast used by infra, platform, and release to make short-term provisioning decisions; numbers will be re-run daily during the first three weeks of rollout and updated with measured cache hit-rate and cold miss metrics.

Unresolved questions / followups:
- Need precise replication factor and shard count for KV cache to convert resident MB -> host count (ask storage infra for shard plan).
- Confirm H100 vs A100 equivalency with hardware team for mixed-batch workloads (we used 0.6x; verify).
- Get a histogram of sequence length per region (assumed 512 tokens) to refine compute estimates.

End of sheet.
